reviewer: Pickle: official-source winter pipe freezing prevention comparison
method: Reviewed the full draft against official sources. Seoul Arisu Waterworks 4-stage meter-freeze advisory (arisu.seoul.go.kr): gwanSim (min temp above -5 C, pre-insulate meter box and exposed pipes), juui (-5 to -10 C, re-check insulation), gyeongGye (-10 to -15 C, open an indoor tap slightly during long absences), simGak (below -15 C, keep a tap trickling even for short absences). Seoul Metropolitan Government announcements on its media hub: 2024-12-03 piece (fill-trickle-thaw three rules; freezing rises when min temp stays below -10 C for 2+ days and surges at -15 C; trickle volume should fill a paper cup in 45 seconds at 0 to -10 C and in 33 seconds below -10 C; 10 hours of trickling costs under 300 KRW per day on the household tariff; last winter Seoul recorded 3,072 meter freezes, 682 in Nowon-gu) and the 2026-01-05 piece (countermeasures through March 15, 24-hour emergency command below -10 C, 300,000 households under special management, 290,000 insulation covers distributed, digital meters rated to survive below -10 C for 24+ hours) and the 2021-11-16 piece (10,895 freezes, 80 percent caused by missing meter-box insulation; open flame risks fire and water above 50 C cracks the meter). MOTIE press release 2023-01-19: self-regulating heating-cable fires average about 300 per year over five years with about 3.3 billion KRW in property damage; of 12 domestic cable makers only 6 (50 percent) had certification; electric-facility technical standards require cables conforming to KS C IEC 60800; the March 2022 Cheongju clinic fire (10 injured, 2 billion KRW damage) originated from an installed self-regulating cable; about 500 sites surveyed. Korea Electrical Safety Corporation figures via Newspim 2022-10-31: about 1,600 heating-cable fires over five years, only 5 certified products on the market, over half of installed cables older than 10 years, recommended service life 7-10 years. Fire science and engineering 2021 (Yu & Jee, Kangwon National University, DOI 10.7731/kifse.f710fe7e): a 15 W/m commercial self-regulating cable rated 65 C continuous / 80 C momentary loses its self-regulating property at 160-170 C, and at 170 C overheat the current spikes more than 20x and ignition occurs within about 15 minutes on average. MOIS detailed cold-wave action guidance on Korea.kr (2024-12-06): fill meter boxes, pipes and boiler piping with insulation and seal the outside with tape; trickle a tap during long absences; thaw frozen pipes with lukewarm water or a hair dryer and never use an open flame; report electrical trouble to KEPCO 123 or KESCO 1588-7500. Repair-cost allocation: Korea Real Estate Board/LH rental dispute mediation case (2022-07-14) for a burst washing-machine cold-water pipe totaling 2,100,000 KRW (300,000 replacement + 1,800,000 compensation to the flooded unit), settled with the landlord paying 1,380,000 and the tenant 720,000, citing Civil Code Articles 623 and 374 and Seoul Central District Court 2015GaDan5019288 (tenant liable when negligent hose management causes the freeze); Supreme Court office commentary (scourt.go.kr): minor repairs are the tenant's, large-scale repairs and replacement of basic facilities (cracks, leaks, boiler failure) are the landlord's under Civil Code 623, with cost recovery under Article 626; Korea Apartment Newspaper case article citing Seoul data (3,621 freezes: 67.7% missing insulation, 24% long absence, 6.5% exposed meter) and a Daejeon judgment ordering the upstairs resident to pay about 10 million KRW including 7.3 million repair cost plus 3 million to the tenant after ignoring trickle notices. Electricity tariff from the Ministry of Government Legislation EasyLaw housing low-voltage table: 910 KRW basic / 120.0 KRW per kWh up to 200 kWh plus 2.7% fund and 10% VAT, a billed rate of about 135.56 (about 136) KRW/kWh. All 12 source URLs returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-31. Derived figures are recorded in the research calculations: trickling at the 33-second paper-cup rate is about 19.6 L per hour and about 196 L over 10 hours (about 0.2 m3), matching Seoul's under-300-KRW-per-day guidance; a 3 W/m sensor-type cable on a 10 m pipe at 24 h draws 0.72 kWh, about 98 KRW per day and about 2,940 KRW per month (30 m: about 294 KRW per day, about 8,820 per month), an upper bound because sensor types cycle; a 10,900 KRW meter cover is about 1/193 of the 2,100,000 KRW burst-pipe mediation case (replacement alone about 28x). The three Coupang affiliate links were generated on 2026-10-31 and verified in-browser to resolve to the correct product pages with the AF6593875 partner tag: Wallseol Korean anti-freeze heating cable, silicone, auto power sensor type, KC certified, 30 m (57,900 KRW, list 75,700, 47 reviews, 220 V, seller Q&A: 3 W per meter, do not overlap or cover the end fittings with water), Sudoworld meter freeze-protection insulation cover (10,900 KRW, list 29,750, 63% off, 35 reviews, 100+ bought last month, rocket shipping), and Toyilon/Artion flame-retardant pipe insulation (15A/25T 9,020 KRW up to 200A 52,780 KRW, seller Daon, 0 reviews). Plan deviations: the plan's 'Seoul Fire Department 100 C overlap overheat' figure could not be verified in any primary source, so the draft uses the peer-reviewed 160-170 C self-regulating failure and 170 C ignition reproduction plus the MOTIE/KESCO fire statistics instead; the plan's 'hair dryer cold/warm air only' rule is presented as the MOIS lukewarm-water-or-hair-dryer guidance with open flame prohibited, noting some local guides classify dryers as open flame; the plan's 'anti-freeze valve' product category is described as a substitute/auxiliary for trickling without a dedicated official citation, and the '500,000 KRW burst repair' hook was replaced with the verified 300,000 KRW replacement and 2,100,000 KRW mediation totals; the 3rd product has zero reviews on its listing, disclosed in the guide section and ranking card wording.
